## Rust frontend parsing

- Assumption: `rust-frontend`

The Rust frontend parses each source into the wire request that the source denotes. The kernel checks every declaration that it receives again, but parser fidelity is tested only.

<a id="assumption.lean-to-c"></a>

## Lean-to-C toolchain and C compiler

- Assumption: `lean-to-c`

The Lean compiler and the C compiler translate generated Lean into native code that computes the Lean definitions. Native refinement is not proved.

No claim cites this assumption.

<a id="assumption.lean-rat-gmp"></a>

## Lean core Rat and GMP

- Assumption: `lean-rat-gmp`

Lean core's `Rat` arithmetic, and the GMP library that implements large numbers, compute the rational and integer operations that the runtime uses.

No claim cites this assumption.

<a id="assumption.mathlib"></a>

## mathlib

- Assumption: `mathlib`

mathlib, at the commit that `lean-bridge/lake-manifest.json` pins, defines the mathematical objects that the bridge theorems use with their standard meaning. The official Lean kernel checks every bridge proof.

<a id="assumption.promotion-reflection"></a>

## Promotion fixture reflection

- Assumption: `promotion-reflection`

`VastitasKernel.IndexedPromotionFixture.checked` is the Core module that `Indexed.LegacySource.check` returns for `tests/fixtures/promotion.json`. The `stdlib_indexed_checked%` elaborator runs that checker at elaboration time, prints the returned module with `reprStr` and elaborates the text as `checked`; before parsing, it writes the field name `end` as `«end»`. A build-time `#eval` compares the two renderings and checks the reflected module again with `Typing.checkModule`. That agreement rests on compiled evaluation and on a faithful `Repr`, which the axiom audit cannot see.
